# 1. Introduction

## 1.1 Background and Use Case

Zurich has a large amount of motorized traffic, and traffic volume changes throughout the day and across locations. Weather conditions may also be associated with changes in traffic volume.

## 1.2 Objectives

The objective of this project is to explore traffic volume in Zurich during 2025 and investigate how traffic volume varies with time, weather conditions and location.

## 1.3 Research Questions

RQ1. Temporal patterns How does traffic volume vary across different times of the day and days of the week in Zurich in 2025?

RQ2. Weather How are weather conditions associated with traffic volume in Zurich in 2025?

RQ3. Location How does traffic volume differ across traffic counting locations and directions in Zurich in 2025?

RQ4.Model To what extent can traffic volume be explained by temporal, weather and location-related variables?

# 2. Data Sources

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
```

## 2.1 Inspecting the Traffic Data

```{r}
traffic <- read.csv("data/sid_dav_verkehrszaehlung_miv_od2031_2025.csv")
```

```{r}
head(traffic, n = 10)
```

The original traffic dataset contains German variable names. Before the analysis, the variables were renamed into English to improve readability and consistency throughout the project.

## 2.2 Renaming and Cleaning Traffic Variables

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
traffic <- traffic %>%
  rename(
    MSID = MSID,
    MSName = MSName,
    ZS_ID = ZSID,
    ZS_Name = ZSName,
    Axis = Achse,
    House_Number = HNr,
    Elevation = Hoehe,
    Easting = EKoord,
    Northing = NKoord,
    Direction = Richtung,
    K_Number = Knummer,
    K_Name = Kname,
    Number_of_Detectors = AnzDetektoren,
    D1_ID = D1ID,
    D2_ID = D2ID,
    D3_ID = D3ID,
    D4_ID = D4ID,
    Measurement_DateTime = MessungDatZeit,
    Delivery_Date = LieferDat,
    Number_of_Vehicles = AnzFahrzeuge,
    Vehicle_Count_Status = AnzFahrzeugeStatus
  )
```

## Trraffic data dictionary

MSID：Unique ID of the measurement station. MSName：Name of the measurement station. ZS_ID：Unique ID of the traffic counting point. ZS_Name:Name of the traffic counting point. Axis: The road axis associated with the traffic counting point. House_Number: House Number - Building/street number of the location. Elevation: Elevation - Height/elevation of the measurement location. Easting: Easting coordinate. Northing: Easting coordinate. Direction: Direction of traffic being measured. K_Number: Road Number. K_Name: Road Name. Number_of_Detectors:Number of Detectors. D1_ID:ID of the first detector. D2_ID:ID of the second detector. D3_ID:ID of the third detector. D4_ID:ID of the fourth detector. Measurement_DateTime: Date and exact time of measurement. Delivery_Date: Date when the measurement data were delivered to the system. Number_of_Vehicles: Number of vehicles detected during the measurement period. Vehicle_Count_Status:Quality or availability of the vehicle count data. (e.g., Gemessen → Measured;Fehlend → Missing;Imputiert → Imputed)

## 2.3 Preparing Traffic Date and Time

Convert the original Measurement_DateTime variable into a POSIXct datetime variable using the Europe/Zurich time zone.

```{r}
traffic <- traffic %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = ymd_hms(
      Measurement_DateTime,
      tz = "Europe/Zurich"
    )
  )
```

Displays the original and converted datetime values side by side to verify that the conversion was performed correctly.

```{r}
head(traffic %>% select(Measurement_DateTime, datetime), 10)
```

Checks the class of the new datetime variable to confirm that it has been successfully converted to POSIXct format.

```{r}
class(traffic$datetime)
```

The original traffic measurement timestamp was converted into a standardized POSIXct datetime format using the Europe/Zurich timezone. A new datetime variable was created for subsequent data integration.

## 2.4 Inspecting and Cleaning the Meteorological/weather Data

```{r}
weather <- read.csv("data/ugz_ogd_meteo_h1_2025.csv")
```

```{r}
head(weather, 10)
```

## 2.5 Renaming and Cleaning Weather Variables

```{r}
weather <- weather %>%
  rename(
    Measurement_DateTime = Datum,
    Location = Standort,
    Parameter = Parameter,
    Interval = Intervall,
    Unit = Einheit,
    Value = Wert,
    Status = Status
  )
```

## Weather data dictionary

Measurement_DateTime:Date and exact time when the weather measurement was taken. Location:Name of the weather station where the measurement was taken. Parameter:Type of weather variable being measured, e.g. temperature, relative humidity, or air pressure. Interval:Time interval over which the weather measurement was recorded, e.g. one hour (h1). Unit:Unit in which the weather parameter is measured, e.g. °C, %, hPa, or m/s. Value Measured Value:Numerical value of the corresponding weather parameter. Status:Status indicating the quality or processing state of the weather measurement.

## 2.6 Preparing Meteorological/weather Date and Time

Convert the original Measurement_DateTime variable from character format into POSIXct datetime format using the Europe/Zurich time zone.

```{r}
weather <- weather %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = as.POSIXct(
      Measurement_DateTime,
      format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M%z",
      tz = "Europe/Zurich"
    )
  )
```

Displays the converted datetime values in a standardized YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format to verify that the date and time were parsed correctly.

```{r}
format(weather$datetime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") %>%
  head(10)
```

Counts missing (NA) values in the new datetime variable to check whether any observations failed to be converted.

```{r}
sum(is.na(weather$datetime))
```

## 2.7 Reshaping the Meteorological Data （long → wide）

```{r}
weather_wide <- weather %>%
  select(
    datetime,
    Location,
    Parameter,
    Value
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Parameter,
    values_from = Value
  )
```

```{r}
head(weather_wide, 10)
```

## 2.8 Checking the Join Keys

Check the time period.

```{r}
range(traffic$datetime, na.rm = TRUE)


```

```{r}
range(weather_wide$datetime, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Both datasets cover the same time period, from 1 January 2025 at 00:00 to 31 December 2025 at 23:00. The timestamps are also represented in the same time zone (CET). Therefore, datetime can be used as a common temporal join key.

```{r}
weather_wide %>%
  count(datetime, Location) %>%
  filter(n > 1)
```
